title: Interleaved scaleup safety-net calculation failure causing transient reserved-pool shortfall
creator: Diego Patel
description: During high-concurrency warmup windows we observed a recurring transient reserved-pool shortfall that caused tenant request failures and automated evictions. The autoscaler attempted multiple concurrent scale-ups for the same pool across overlapping allocation epochs; the safety-net calculation that reserves headroom for warm requests was applied twice and then incorrectly subtracted when both scale-ups completed, leaving the pool in an undersized state for ~20-90s. Several enterprise customers reported 5-15% increased 429/503 errors during peak bursts. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a targeted bugfix to the scale controller's epoch accounting logic.
reproduction_steps: Simulate 200 concurrent bursty tenants hitting a reserved pool with warmup=enabled and burst_limit configured
Force two autoscaler leaders to schedule overlapping scale-up operations by delaying leader heartbeats in one region (test harness available)
Observe safety-net headroom metric (autoscaler.pool.<id>.safety_net_reserved) being added twice then removed once
Verify pool.available_slots decreases below expected capacity and requests are rejected with allocation failure logs
investigation_summary: Telemetry shows three correlated signals: 1) overlapping scale-up transactions with identical target_size, 2) a non-idempotent safety-net update path that uses a transient epoch token, and 3) a delayed background reconciliation that removed leftover safety-net entries after scale-ups completed. Reproducible in staging with race-injection. Heap of controller logs attached. No kernel-level or device failures observed.
root_cause: A race in the scale controller: concurrent scale-up transactions used a non-atomic safety-net delta update that relied on a per-epoch ephemeral token. When two scale-ups interleaved, the second update interpreted the token as not-yet-applied and applied a second reservation. Later a reconciliation job that assumed single application removed a single reservation, leaving the pool under-reserved. The reconciliation logic lacked the idempotency guards required for concurrent scale operations.
mitigation: Hotfix: disable background reconciliation for safety-net entries until the controller implements idempotent delta application (rolled to prod within 90 minutes)
Emergency: increase pool soft-capacity by +15% for affected tenants to mask transient shortfall
Customer comms: sent targeted incident emails to impacted customers and opened support tickets for OptimaDocs and MeridianPay
proposed_fix: Implement atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) semantics for safety-net delta updates keyed by scale-operation-id and epoch. Introduce server-side idempotency token persisted in controller state and add unit + race tests to verify behavior under concurrent leaders. Add a reconciliation audit that logs mismatches without removing entries until verified.
implementation_notes: Patch will modify scale-controller transactions in controller/core/scale_ops.go and add persistent operation metadata to the controller KV. Add integration test that injects leader-flap and verifies safety-net metrics remain stable. Expect ~3-day development + 1-day rollout to canary then region-by-region.
